summary: Iteration-2 testing: extended backend_test.py with 14 new tests covering Notes, Pinned Topics, signed Manifest (export/import/tamper/schema/signature), and PWA static assets. Also drove the UI via Playwright across Dashboard (ManifestCard + hero-pinned-link + nav-pinned), /pinned (edit/add seed/save), and /phase/0 (notes drawer autosave). 29/31 backend tests pass. The 2 failures (notes persistence + manifest-notes passthrough) share the same root cause: a Mongo dot-notation bug in POST /api/sessions/{id}/notes. Frontend wired correctly except note-preview reflects the same backend bug.

critical.issue: Step IDs contain '.' (e.g. '0.1'). Backend uses $set: {f'notes.{step_id}': note}, which Mongo interprets as a nested path. Result: a POST with step_id='0.1' stores notes = {"0": {"1": "..."}} instead of notes = {"0.1": "..."}. Verified live via curl: response contains "notes": {"0": {"1": "hello"}}. This breaks (a) GET /api/sessions/{id}.notes[step_id], (b) manifest export (session.notes map), (c) frontend note-preview-{step_id} rendering (lookup fails).

ui_bugs.issue: After typing in notes-textarea-0.1, closing the drawer, and reopening the page, the note-preview-0.1 element never renders. Root cause is the backend Mongo dot-notation bug above (notes["0.1"] does not exist; it is stored nested). UI code is otherwise correct.

action_items: Fix notes persistence: do NOT use step_id directly as a Mongo field name. Options: (1) replace '.' with a safe char when building the $set key (e.g. step_id.replace('.', '_')) and reverse on read; (2) fetch doc, mutate dict in Python, write back with full notes map; (3) store notes as an array of {step_id, note} objects. Apply the same transform in the manifest export/import to keep round-trip consistent.
After fix, re-run TestNotes.test_set_note_and_persist and TestManifest.test_export_manifest; both should go green and note-preview-0.1 will show on the UI without any frontend change.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: SIGNING_KEY read at import time without fallback — OK for required-env hygiene, but ensure prod sets TORUS_SIGNING_KEY or the backend will fail to start.
server.py: import json inside functions (export_manifest, import_manifest) — minor; move to module scope.

server.py: default pinned topics are returned from GET /pinned when pinned_topics is empty, but PUT with empty list stores [] and GET will then re-show defaults. Semantics of 'user cleared all topics' are ambiguous — consider using None vs [] or a 'has_pinned' flag.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all testids present; note-preview blocked by backend bug)

seed_data_creation: Transient sessions created per test run (TEST_ prefixed profile/topics/notes). No long-lived seed required.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The only outstanding defect is the Mongo dot-notation issue in POST /api/sessions/{id}/notes. All PWA assets (manifest.webmanifest, service-worker.js, torus-icon.svg) are served correctly from the frontend origin. Manifest export/import round-trip and signature tamper detection work. Pinned Topics CRUD + YAML download work. Frontend testids all present: manifest-card, export-manifest-btn (links to /api/sessions/{id}/manifest), import-manifest-btn, hero-pinned-link, nav-pinned, pinned-header, pinned-topic-0, topic-name-0, seed-input-0-0/0-1, add-topic-btn, add-seed-0, save-pinned-btn (toast 'Pinned topics saved' confirmed), download-pinned-btn, notes-btn-0.1, notes-textarea-0.1, notes-close-0.1.
rca of the issue: RCA — notes persistence: In backend/server.py set_note() uses `{"$set": {f"notes.{body.step_id}": body.note}}`. MongoDB interprets '.' in field paths as sub-document traversal. Phase step IDs like '0.1', '0.2', ... therefore become nested keys (notes.0.1 → notes['0']['1']). Reproduction: POST /api/sessions/{id}/notes {step_id:'0.1', note:'hello'} → GET /api/sessions/{id} returns notes={"0":{"1":"hello"}}. Impact: notes do not round-trip, manifest export is lossy, frontend note preview never renders. Mitigation: sanitize the key before $set (e.g., replace '.' with '_' or '::') and reverse in all read paths (GET session, manifest export, manifest import); or store notes as a sub-array of {step_id, note} objects.
